basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 8.' and it opens 'Vers. 8. Fratres enim sumus. Tribus enim modis in Scriptura sancta fratres vocantur:'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 8. Fratres enim sumus. Tribus enim modis in Scriptura sancta fratres vocantur: natura, sicut Jacob et Isaac: cognatione, sicut Abraham et Lot; Lot enim filius fuerat fratris sui Aran: gente, sicut omnes Judaei fratres dicuntur, dicente lege: Si attenuatus frater tuus Hebraeus vendiderit se tibi (Levit. XXV, 25). Et attendendum quanta cura concordiae sancto viro fuerit propter quam custodiendam optionem | dedit Lot, ut aut ipse pergeret illo remanente, aut certe, si ipse alibi vellet recedere, ipse ibi maneret
